thesis: The 60-day decline follows a confirmed, company-disclosed structural event: an upsized $20B common-stock offering that closed August 12, 2026, issuing roughly 210.5 million new shares at $95, which Bank of America estimates reduces future EPS by 4-5%. The stock closed at $90.07 on August 21, below that offering price. Contributing but not clearly dominant factors include a UBS price-target cut to $112 (Neutral maintained), continued heavy Foundry losses, and a broad semiconductor drawdown alongside rising Treasury yields — no single driver fully accounts for the 32% move. A US Supreme Court oral argument in the Intel 401(k) case is scheduled for October, an unresolved event inside the next 90 days. This suggests the dilution is a disclosed, permanent change to the share count rather than a temporary sentiment swing, which argues against opening a new position here.
invalidation: Foundry losses narrow materially in Q3 results, or the stock reclaims and holds the $95 offering price on disclosed operating progress rather than on sector beta.
sources: Intel Corp SEC Form DEF 14A FY2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000061/intc_courtesy-pdfa.pdf

thesis: Marvell fell 37% in July as investors sold AI and semiconductor names broadly on skepticism that the AI capex wave will pay off — a sector-wide driver rather than a company-specific disclosure. Company-level evidence is mixed and offsetting: reports that Amazon may have shifted next-generation Trainium design work to a competitor weigh against an expanded long-term custom-silicon partnership with Alphabet's Google that JPMorgan called a 'clear positive', while the June 4 all-time closing high of $316.43 followed NVIDIA's CEO calling Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex — an outside opinion, not a company disclosure. Q2 results land August 27, three days out, against guidance for 35% revenue growth to $2.7B and non-GAAP EPS of $0.93 — an unresolved binary event that could reverse the read in either direction. This suggests waiting for the print rather than entering ahead of it.
invalidation: August 27 results confirm custom-silicon design-win losses, or revenue guidance falls materially short of the 35% growth midpoint.
sources: SEC (Marvell FY2025 annual report, no restatement/indictment disclosed): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1835632/000110465925043094/tm252448d7_ars.pdf

thesis: Fiscal Q3 2026 (June quarter) delivered confirmed, company-disclosed record results: revenue of $109.42B (+16.4%), EPS of $2.02 against a $1.89 consensus, iPhone revenue of $54.25B and Services at an all-time high of $30.74B, alongside a newly authorized $100B buyback. The strongest counter-evidence is the more cautious forward revenue outlook and the open debate over Apple's AI strategy, which together drove roughly a 10% pullback from the late-July record above $340 — but that does not change the read, because the caution concerns the pace of the coming quarter while the disclosed June-quarter cash generation and the already-approved repurchase authorization are settled facts, and the shares sit about 9% below the 52-week high rather than at a stretched level. On litigation, the DOJ antitrust case has no trial date, is in early settlement talks, and is not expected to reach trial before 2027, so no scheduled ruling falls in the next 90 days. This suggests the pullback repriced expectations rather than the disclosed business.
invalidation: Fiscal Q4 (September quarter) results in late October show Services growth decelerating from the record $30.74B run-rate, or the $100B repurchase authorization goes unexecuted.
sources: Bloomberg (DOJ settlement talks, no trial date): https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-17/apple-in-early-settlement-talks-with-doj-over-antitrust-case
Apple Inc. SEC Form DEF 14A FY2026 (EY reappointed; planned PAO transition): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000130817926000008/aapl_courtesy-pdf.pdf

thesis: Q2 2026 results reported August 4 beat on both lines — EPS of $1.66 against $1.62 consensus and revenue of $11.55B against $11.28B — yet the stock still sold off, and July's 18% decline is attributed to a broad chip-sector drawdown as investors turned skeptical on AI spending rather than to any disclosed deterioration at AMD. Coverage frames the negative reaction explicitly as an expectations problem after a roughly 140% year-to-date run, not a results problem, which makes the move sentiment-driven rather than a fundamental change. No lawsuit or investigation with a scheduled ruling, hearing, or deadline in the next 90 days surfaced, and no restatement, auditor dismissal, or executive indictment in the last three years surfaced. This suggests the disclosed business is intact while the multiple compresses, but with a sector-wide driver the read is not company-specific enough to carry conviction.
invalidation: Q3 2026 results or guidance show data-center revenue growth decelerating, or the stock loses its 200-day moving average near $330.

thesis: SpaceX listed on Nasdaq June 12, 2026 at $135 and traded down more than 40% from its immediate post-IPO peak. The drivers are identifiable but largely mechanical and supply-related: a $60B all-stock acquisition of Cursor announced days after listing that diluted holders into early post-IPO selling pressure, and a staggered lockup that has already released roughly 319 million shares and will free about 88% of the ~13 billion share count through 2027. One company-specific operational setback also contributed — the July 16 Starship launch was aborted after several engines failed. Shares have since recovered back above the $135 IPO price. Texas property-owner suits filed April 30, 2026 over Starship acoustic damage are pending with no scheduled ruling or trial date found in the next 90 days. With most of the float still scheduled to unlock through 2027, the dominant driver is share supply rather than a resolved fundamental change, which suggests a persistent overhang rather than a clean entry.
invalidation: A successful Starship flight plus a lockup tranche absorbed without the stock breaking back below the $135 IPO price would weaken the supply-overhang read.
sources: Bloomberg Law / OpenClassActions (Texas property-owner suits, no scheduled date): https://openclassactions.com/blog/spacex-class-action-lawsuits-2026.php
